claims.text: Lithographic patterning of continuous FeMnNiGeSi-type alloy films into nanoribbons alters their mesoscale magnetic-domain structure.
Lithographic patterning into nanoribbons alters the grain-boundary structure of the films.
The altered domain and grain-boundary structures modulate the magnetocaloric response.
The altered domain and grain-boundary structures reduce hysteresis during low-field magnetic-cooling cycles.
Patterning a continuous thin film into nanoribbons imposes additional nanoscale grain boundaries.
Nanoribbon patterning introduces edge effects at the nanoribbon boundaries.
Modified magnetic-domain sizes and enhanced boundary effects influence domain nucleation and transformation kinetics.
Interrupting domain continuity reduces cooperative long-range magnetostructural transitions.
Reduced cooperativity lowers the energy barrier for magnetic reorientation.
Nanostructuring changes the latent-heat release profile.
Patterned nanoribbons will have a smaller hysteresis width than the as-deposited continuous-film baseline during otherwise identical low-field cycling.
Patterned nanoribbons may have a lower peak magnetocaloric-response magnitude than the continuous-film baseline.
Patterned nanoribbons may exhibit a shift in phase-transition temperature relative to the continuous-film baseline.
Bulk forms of the alloy exhibit a notable magnetocaloric response accompanied by hysteresis.
Heat-transfer rate limits the applicable magnetic-cooling cycle frequency.
The predicted patterning effects need not extrapolate to high-field, high-frequency, or bulk unpatterned regimes.
